title: Qualcomm to Acquire PickNik to Advance the Future of Open Robotics and Physical AI
summary: Qualcomm is acquiring PickNik, the company behind MoveIt, to bring the widely used open-source manipulation framework into tighter alignment with Qualcomm Dragonwing Robotics and Arduino platforms. The move is meant to make advanced robot manipulation easier to deploy on edge AI and heterogeneous compute hardware, potentially giving a large developer base a smoother path from open robotics software to physical AI systems.

extra.full_text: MoveIt, one of the most widely used open-source robotics manipulation frameworks, is expected to offer streamlined integration with Qualcomm® Dragonwing™ Robotics platforms and Arduino® platforms, expanding access to advanced robotics, and aiming to enable millions of developers to leverage edge AI and heterogeneous compute to build the next generation of intelligent robots.

title: MES Inc. Urges Robotics OEMs to Lock In Manufacturing Strategy Before Design Freeze as Global Robot Demand Hits Record Levels
summary: MES Inc. is warning robotics OEMs to settle their manufacturing and sourcing strategy before design freeze, arguing that structural aluminum components will strongly affect how quickly humanoid, mobile, and collaborative robots can move from prototypes into volume production. The company frames this as a scaling bottleneck at a moment when global industrial robot installations have stayed above 500,000 units for four straight years, making supply-chain readiness and component manufacturability central to meeting record demand.

title: We trained a robot to play football
summary: Skild AI trained a football-playing robot through physical self-play: 140 simulated years of matches against progressively stronger opponents, each drawn from earlier versions of the same model. The pitch is that AlphaGo-style self-play can produce emergent, highly capable behavior not just in games, but in embodied robots that have to execute skills under real physical dynamics.

extra.full_text: We trained a robot to play football. How? Self-play for 140 years in a virtual World Cup. It was born in a physics simulation. For 140 years, our model played against increasingly tough opponents, each one a previous version of itself. Once it was ready, we challenged it to a match. ⚽ AlphaGo taught us that self-play can lead to emergent, superhuman behavior. We're bringing it to the physical world. title: Physical Self-Play
summary: Physical Self-Play shows a strong physical-AI base model, S1, being post-trained through self-play in simulation, where it improves by competing against copies of itself. The striking result is that this process can produce highly dexterous, dynamic behavior such as playing soccer, suggesting self-play may be a practical route for turning general robot policies into agents that handle fast, contact-rich skills.

extra.full_text: A breakthrough post-training result for physical AI via self-play: a strong base model like S1 can learn to complete extremely dexterous and dynamic tasks, like soccer, by competing against itself in a simulation.

title: KAIST, 세계 최초 풀코스 마라톤 완주한 ‘로봇 설계 원리’ 발표
summary: KAIST reported the design principles behind RAIBO2, a quadruped robot that completed a full 42.195 km marathon at the Sangju Gotgam Marathon in November 2024 without battery charging or replacement. The Nature-published work centers on the robot’s long-distance running system, showing that legged robots can sustain real outdoor endurance performance rather than short lab demonstrations, with KAIST aiming to extend the technology toward mass-producible industrial robots.

title: MVP Robotics Demonstrates Heavy-Payload Autonomy in Wildfire Ground Vehicle Challenge
summary: MVP Robotics demonstrated its M2P Heavy ground vehicle in an autonomous wildfire-response field challenge, moving payloads of up to 800 pounds across demanding terrain. The result points to a practical role for heavy-load robotic vehicles in fireground logistics, where carrying equipment or supplies through hazardous terrain can reduce risk and workload for human crews.

title: PitPro’s first tire-changing robot goes live in Canada
summary: PitPro has deployed its first automated tire-changing robot in Canada, with the startup claiming the system can swap all four tires in under 15 minutes. The launch matters because tire service is a repetitive, labor-intensive garage workflow where speed and consistency are commercially valuable, and this gives a concrete early example of robotics moving into routine automotive maintenance.

title: 구테흐스 UN 사무총장, “AI에 생사 결정 맡겨선 안 돼”…킬러 로봇 금지 촉구
summary: António Guterres used his annual UN General Assembly report to warn that AI and autonomous weapons are becoming a core test of global power, alongside war, inequality, and climate change. He called for keeping AI out of life-and-death decisions and building an international AI risk-management system with independent oversight, framing “killer robots” as a governance problem that could deepen geopolitical fragmentation if left unchecked.

title: 엔도로보틱스, IPO 시동…미래에셋증권 대표주관사 우선협상자 선정
summary: Endorobotics, a Korean startup developing flexible endoscopic surgical robots, has chosen Mirae Asset Securities as the preferred lead underwriter as it begins preparing for an IPO targeted for the second half of 2028. The company was founded in 2019 around core technology transferred from work begun in 2012 by CEO Kim Byung-gon and Korea University professor Hong Dae-hee’s team, supported by Korea’s ICT ministry and National Research Foundation.
